answer: At the network’s orchard of reputation, each new agent must first earn a signal from a trusted summit node by completing a verifiable task; the node issues a signed credential that ages over time. When voting, the protocol applies quadratic weighting: one credential counts as one vote, while k fresh credentials together count only √k, so a swarm of Sybil identities adds negligible influence. An attacker therefore must acquire long‑lived credentials from summit nodes, a cost that grows linearly with the desired influence rather than with the number of fake accounts.
